source1: François Vallat, 'Elam i. The history of Elam', Encyclopaedia Iranica VIII/3, 1998 - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/elam-i
source2: Muhammad A. Dandamayev, 'Cyrus iii. Cyrus II the Great', Encyclopaedia Iranica - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/cyrus-iii
notes: Vallat: after 646 Elamite royalty fragmented among small kingdoms; Susiana conquered by Achaemenids, perhaps Cyrus 539. Dandamayev: Elam conquered, timing debated (before or after Babylon's fall). Anshan Persians external to Susa at W start.

Hittite raid ended Hammurabi's dynasty c. 1595 BCE (middle chronology), a temporary conquest; Kassites took Babylon later, timing unclear, possible Sealand role debated. Zadok names Telipinu, likely slip. No documented crisis 1645-1595.

source1: P.K. Bhattacharyya, 'Shashanka', Banglapedia: National Encyclopedia of Bangladesh, Asiatic Society of Bangladesh - https://en.banglapedia.org/index.php/Shashanka
source2: Suchandra Ghosh, 'Karnasuvarna', Banglapedia, Asiatic Society of Bangladesh - https://en.banglapedia.org/index.php/Karnasuvarna
notes: After Shashanka (r. c. 600-625) Gauda power declined; Bhaskaravarman of Kamarupa conquered capital Karnasuvarna (Nidhanpur grant from its victory camp), perhaps briefly; Jayanaga later ruled there. Conquest date uncertain (625-640s). Khadga ruled east Bengal, not core.

source1: Alejandro Pastrana and Patricia Fournier, 'Cuicuilco', Oxford Encyclopedia of Mesoamerican Cultures vol. 1, Oxford University Press 2001 - https://www.academia.edu/1041780/
source2: George L. Cowgill, 'State and Society at Teotihuacan, Mexico', Annual Review of Anthropology 26, 1997 (abstract) - https://www.annualreviews.org/doi/10.1146/annurev.anthro.26.1.129
notes: Archaeological phase: several Late Formative centres (Cuicuilco, Teotihuacan) as chiefdoms, no recorded central authority. Cuicuilco continued past 100 BCE until Xitle eruption; basin population relocated into Teotihuacan 100 BCE-200 CE, indicating continuity, not replacement.

source2: J.B. Bury, History of the Later Roman Empire vol. I ch. 12, Macmillan 1923 - https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/E/Roman/Texts/secondary/BURLAT/12*.html
notes: Odoacer's kingdom (kept Roman administration) invaded 489 by Theodoric's Ostrogoths from Moesia on Zeno's order; three defeats, Ravenna besieged, surrendered and Odoacer killed March 493. Q4 Y: 472-476 coups and 476 army revolt. End 493, not 489.

successor: Cahokia - Middle Woodland (American Bottom Cement Hollow/Holding phases)
source1: Andrew C. Fortier, Selected Sites in the Hill Lake Locality, FAI-270 Site Reports vol. 13, Illinois State Archaeological Survey (catalogue summary) - https://www.isas.illinois.edu/publications/fai-270
source2: Andrew C. Fortier, The Petite Michele Site: An Early Middle Woodland Occupation in the American Bottom, ISAS Research Reports 19, 2004 (catalogue summary) - https://www.isas.illinois.edu/publications/research_reports
notes: Archaeological phase. ISAS summaries note a locality 'cultural continuum' and southern ties in Cement Hollow phase; Fortier's synthesis (not opened) reportedly stresses discontinuous, intrusive Early and Middle Woodland complexes. Continuity versus replacement unresolved.

successor: Kingdom of Poland (Jadwiga; Jagiellonian Poland-Lithuania from 1386)
notes: Polish Crown continued without break: Piast line ended 1370, Angevin Louis ruled to 1382, Polish lords chose Jadwiga (crowned 1384), then elected Jogaila 1386 (Krewo personal union). Q4 Y: 1382-85 interregnum strife, rival claimants.

source2: Rüdiger Schmitt, 'Artaxerxes III', Encyclopaedia Iranica II/6, 1986 - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/artaxerxes-iii
notes: Artaxerxes III invaded via Nile mouths, took Pelusium and Bubastis, reconquest complete c. 343 BCE; Nectanebo II fled to Upper Egypt or Nubia. Q4 Y: Nectanebo usurped throne from Tachos c. 360; rival pretender nearly overthrew him.

successor: Constitutional Siam under the People's Party (Khana Ratsadon)
notes: 24 June 1932 bloodless coup by People's Party officials forced a constitution, ending absolute monarchy; king kept throne. Listed Vietnamese candidates irrelevant. Q4 Y: 1901-02 Holy Man's and Phrae revolts, 1912 officers' plot.
